title: Who Will Go?
question: What makes Isaiah ready to answer "Here am I; send me"?
blurb: A holy God asks who will go, and one cleansed man dares to volunteer. What got him there?

nodes.content: What makes Isaiah ready to answer "Here am I; send me"?

nodes.verseText: Then I heard the voice of the Lord saying: “Whom shall I send? Who will go for Us?” And I said: “Here am I. Send me!”

nodes.content: Just before this, Isaiah cried 'Woe is me, for I am ruined' when he saw the King, the LORD of Hosts (Isaiah 6:5). His readiness follows being undone, not feeling worthy.

nodes.verseText: And with it he touched my mouth and said: “Now that this has touched your lips, your iniquity is removed and your sin is atoned for.”
Therefore, go! I am sending you to Pharaoh to bring My people the Israelites out of Egypt.”
Therefore go and make disciples of all nations, baptizing them in the name of the Father and of the Son and of the Holy Spirit,

nodes.content: God asks 'Who will go for Us?' and Isaiah freely offers himself: 'Here am I. Send me!' His answer is willing surrender, not coercion.
